sara (People Ops): Quick q for managers: how are you handling mid-cycle comp decisions for ICs who converted from contractor->FTE last quarter? Need to standardize effective dates and retro pay rules.

nina (Eng Manager): We ran into this last month. Our approach was: 1) set FTE base on conversion date, 2) for promo/leveling we consider only FTE time for eligibility, 3) retro pay for market adjustments handled as one-time lump sum if approved.

raj (IC): So if I converted Jan 5 and started doing higher-scope work Feb 1, do I have to wait a full cycle?

sara (People Ops): Good question. Policy draft: eligible after 90 days as FTE for routine promotions; exceptions allowed for clear retention cases. If promotion is approved earlier, effective date = promotion approval date and retro amount = pro-rated base delta back to conversion date (people ops will calculate payroll adjustments).

comp-bot: :info: FYI — payroll cutoff is the 15th for end-of-month changes. Requests approved after cutoff go in next payroll cycle (https://go.company/payroll-dates).

nina (Eng Manager): For exceptions (retention), what documentation do you want?

sara (People Ops): Short manager note + evidence. Include: 1) why retention is needed (offer on table or high flight risk), 2) short timeline, 3) suggested comp target and range, 4) approval path (director sign-off). We triage these within 48 hours.

raj (IC): Can managers request equity acceleration on conversions? My equity grant vests later than my peers.

tom (Recruiter): Equity changes for conversions go through Recruiting + People Ops comp. We treat conversion grants as typical new-hire grants; accelerations are rare but possible for strong retention cases. Submit the manager rationale and recruiting will advise market comps.

nina (Eng Manager): Practical ask: can we backdate title changes? We sometimes want the title to reflect work starting earlier than the paperwork.

sara (People Ops): Titles can be backdated up to 30 days with proper manager note and org approval. For >30 days, need director+HRBP signoff and a clear business justification. Payroll/HR systems will reflect the official effective date; badges and org chart can show the earlier start only with approval.

raj (IC): What's the comms cadence? If approved, do we tell the whole company or just the team?

sara (People Ops): Standard: manager tells the person first. Company-wide announcement only for promotions at senior+ bands or public recognition. For comp changes we do not announce amounts publicly. We can provide a suggested manager script.

nina (Eng Manager): Could we get a template for manager script + an email for redirecting comp questions to People Ops? Saves awkward replies.

sara (People Ops): Yes — I'll post templates in the promo toolkit and link here. Example manager script (short):

```
Hi <name>, congrats — effective <date> you've been promoted to <new title>. This reflects sustained contributions in <area>. People Ops will follow up on compensation details. I'm available to discuss questions.
```

comp-bot: :white_check_mark: Promo toolkit link saved: https://go.company/promo-toolkit (last updated 2026-03-12)

sara (People Ops): Last note on approvals: manager -> director -> People Ops comp -> payroll. If you need an expedited path (offer counter within 48h), tag me + your director in the nomination form.

nina (Eng Manager): Thanks — helpful. I'll start using the 90-day rule and ping for any retention exceptions.

raj (IC): Appreciate the clarity. I'll check with my manager about the conversion equity question.

sara (People Ops): Great. I'll upload the formal mini-policy and templates by EOD tomorrow. DM me if you have an active case and need help.
